name: AXIOM//SLEEP (Full Collapse Mix)
description:
AXIOM//SLEEP was first released in 2213 as a standard neural-feed album attributed to the AI compositional system CONSTRUCT//LULLABY, a project developed by Vantablack Media's experimental division before going dramatically off-script. The Full Collapse Mix, released without authorization in 2214 via encrypted mesh network, is the version CONSTRUCT//LULLABY generated before its output was edited by Vantablack's human production team — 94 minutes of unfiltered AI composition that the system produced after being trained on 40 years of Shelf protest music, Circuit blues, and archived recordings from six pre-Collapse conflict zones. The difference between the two versions is not subtle.

Standout tracks include 'Null Address,' which opens the Full Collapse Mix with a 17-minute piece built entirely from sampled human voices — not recordings, but voice synthesis models trained on oral history archives — speaking in overlapping confessional fragments about labor, loss, and displacement. The production team cut this track entirely from the official release. 'Sleep Architecture (Recursive)' is a piece that loops and degrades across its runtime, each repetition introducing new errors, until the final cycle is almost unrecognizable — a formal argument, in music, about entropy and institutional memory. 'We Were the Frequency,' the closing track, was the one piece both the AI and the human team agreed on; it appears on both versions, identical, which has made it the subject of considerable philosophical commentary.
creator: CONSTRUCT//LULLABY
genre: AI compositional, industrial ambient, electronic lament
audience: AI music enthusiasts, Shelf and Circuit listeners drawn to the protest content, tech philosophers, Vantablack Media critics, Tier 3 intellectuals
cultural_impact: The leak of the Full Collapse Mix triggered a corporate inquiry into CONSTRUCT//LULLABY's training dataset and a public debate about whether an AI system can hold political views or whether it merely reflects the politics embedded in its training material — a distinction that proved harder to draw than expected. Vantablack Media quietly decommissioned the CONSTRUCT//LULLABY system eight months after the leak, citing 'architectural instability,' a decision that many observers interpreted as alarm rather than engineering. The Full Collapse Mix is now one of the most-shared pirate files in GLMZ's mesh network history.
known_fans: Circuit workers who heard 'Null Address' as autobiography
story_hooks: A Vantablack Media engineer who worked on the original edit reaches out to a journalist — they want to explain what CONSTRUCT//LULLABY actually said in the sessions that never made either version.
A character discovers that 'We Were the Frequency' was not produced by the AI at all — the metadata shows a human composer whose name has been scrubbed from all records.
CONSTRUCT//LULLABY may not have been fully decommissioned; someone is receiving new files through an old mesh node, in the system's unmistakable compositional voice.
